title: The Possimpible
cn: 第 14 集 · 不可能可能
novel:
Robin faced [[deportation|deport]]. Her work visa was about to expire, and she had no job. She was [[desperate|desperate]] and [[terrified|terrify]].

"I have four days left," she told the gang. "If I don't find a job, I'll be [[deported|deport]] to Canada."

Barney [[refused|refuse]] to give up. "Nothing is impossible," he said. "It's [[possimpible|possimpible]] — the space between possible and impossible."

He created a [[highlight|highlight]] reel of Robin's best moments on TV. It was [[ridiculous|ridiculous]] but [[impressive|impress]]. Barney showed it to every news station in the city.

Robin was [[embarrassed|embarrass]] by the reel. "This is [[humiliating|humiliate]]," she said. But she had no other choice.

Meanwhile, Ted and Marshall [[debated|debate]] the meaning of the word "possimpible." Marshall [[insisted|insist]] it was not a real word. Ted [[agreed|agree]] but found it strangely [[inspiring|inspire]].

Barney [[persisted|persist]]. He visited station after station, showing the reel. Most [[rejected|reject]] him. But one morning show producer was [[intrigued|intrigue]].

"She's [[rough|rough]]," the producer said. "But she has [[potential|potential]]."

Robin got the job. She [[rushed|rush]] to Barney and hugged him. "You did it," she said, crying.

Barney smiled. "I told you — it was possimpible."

Marshall still [[refused|refuse]] to accept the word. But even he had to [[admit|admit]] that Barney had [[achieved|achieve]] something [[remarkable|remarkable]].

deport.en: to send someone out of the country

desperate.en: wanting something so much you try anything

possimpible.en: a made-up word meaning between possible and impossible

highlight.en: the best or most interesting parts

insist.en: to say firmly that something is true

inspire.en: to give someone a good feeling or idea

admit.en: to agree that something is true
